input.command:
cd /workspace/work/tig/074c-claude-raptor-colab; mkdir -p scripts; cp work/raptor.py scripts/; cp -r work/results results; rm -f results/colab_new_time.txt
cat > results/summary.md <<'E'
# #074 RAPTOR vs flat chunks on QuALITY

GPU: Colab L4. Reader/summariser: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (4B, fp16, no thinking; answer = argmax logit over A-D). Embeddings: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (33M). Data: emozilla/quality validation, 8 articles (seed 0), 145 questions.

| Arm | Accuracy | n | Mean context tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| zero-context | 39.3% | 145 | 0 |
| flat (100-word chunks, top-k, 1500-tok budget) | 66.9% | 145 | 1471 |
| raptor (collapsed tree, 1500-tok budget) | 66.9% | 145 | 1475 |
| full article | 75.2% | 145 | 4958 |

Tree build: 245 s total, 82 summary calls (nodes by level: 299 leaves, 63, 14, 5). KMeans groups of ~5, up to 3 summary levels.

GPU time: ~21.6 min (session created ~03:39 IST, stopped 04:00:37 IST) ≈ 0.55 CU (21.6/60 x 1.54). Balance after stop: 187.28 CU. Session confirmed gone via `colab sessions`.
Caveat: 145 questions, 8 articles; 95% CI is about ±8 pts, so flat = raptor is a tie.
E
cat > chart.py <<'E'
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg'); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
a=['zero','flat','raptor','full'];v=[39.3,66.9,66.9,75.2]
plt.bar(a,v,color=['#999','#4c78a8','#f58518','#54a24b']);plt.ylabel('QuALITY accuracy (%)');plt.title('Qwen3-4B, 145 questions, 8 articles')
for i,x in enumerate(v):plt.text(i,x+1,f'{x}',ha='center')
plt.savefig('chart.png',dpi=120)
E
(python3 chart.py || /workspace/tools/mlenv/bin/python chart.py) 2>&1|tail -2; mv chart.py scripts/; ls
cat > README.md <<'E'
# #074 RAPTOR summaries vs flat chunks (QuALITY)

**Result:** with the same ~1,500-token context budget, RAPTOR-style collapsed-tree retrieval and flat chunk retrieval tie at **66.9%** (97/145). Zero context gets 39.3%, the full article (~5K tokens) 75.2%. Tree building cost 245 s and 82 summary calls for 8 articles, with no accuracy gain here.

![chart](chart.png)

| Arm | Acc | n | Mean ctx tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| zero | 39.3% | 145 | 0 |
| flat | 66.9% | 145 | 1471 |
| raptor | 66.9% | 145 | 1475 |
| full | 75.2% | 145 | 4958 |

## Setup
- Data: `emozilla/quality` validation, 8 articles (seed 0), all 145 questions.
- Reader/summariser: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 fp16; embeddings BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5; KMeans (~5 per cluster), 3 summary levels.
- GPU: Colab L4, ~21.6 min, ≈0.55 CU (minutes/60 x 1.54).
- Reproduce: run `scripts/raptor.py` on a GPU (`NART=8`); writes `runs.json`. Raw outputs in `results/`.
- Costs: the Claude driver's API cost is not measured; any figure would be an API-equivalent estimate only.
- Caveat: small sample (±8 pts CI), articles are short-ish (~2-5K words), 4B reader.
E
cat > writeup.md <<'E'
# Does a RAPTOR summary tree beat plain chunks? Not for QuALITY with a 4B reader

I tested RAPTOR-style retrieval against flat 100-word chunks on 145 QuALITY questions over 8 long articles. Both arms got the same ~1,500-token context and the same Qwen3-4B reader.

Result: a dead tie at 66.9%. Zero context scored 39.3% and the whole article scored 75.2%, so retrieval recovers most of the gap but not all of it.

Building the trees took 245 s (82 summarisation calls) on an L4. That's real overhead for no measured gain. The summaries did enter the top-k, but they displaced chunks rather than adding information, and QuALITY questions often hinge on details that summaries drop.

Caveats: 145 questions give roughly ±8 points of noise, the articles are only a few thousand words (the full text fits in context), and a 4B model writes mediocre summaries. RAPTOR may pay off for much longer documents or thematic questions. This test can't show that.

Code and raw predictions are in the repo.
E
git init -q 2>&1|tail -1; git add -A; git commit -qm "#074 RAPTOR vs flat chunks on QuALITY (Colab L4)" && git log --oneline

I tested RAPTOR-style retrieval against flat 100-word chunks on 145 QuALITY questions over 8 long articles. Both arms got the same ~1,500-token context and the same Qwen3-4B reader.

Result: a dead tie at 66.9%. Zero context scored 39.3% and the whole article scored 75.2%, so retrieval recovers most of the gap but not all of it.

Building the trees took 245 s (82 summarisation calls) on an L4. That's real overhead for no measured gain. The summaries did enter the top-k, but they displaced chunks rather than adding information, and QuALITY questions often hinge on details that summaries drop.

Caveats: 145 questions give roughly ±8 points of noise, the articles are only a few thousand words (the full text fits in context), and a 4B model writes mediocre summaries. RAPTOR may pay off for much longer documents or thematic questions. This test can't show that.

Code and raw predictions are in the repo.
